text:
support-ops: FYI – Customer acme-corp on Dedicated pool `us-west-2-prod` reporting big throughput drop and a lot of 429s since ~09:10 UTC. SLO alerts firing. Can eng-runtime take a look?

jess (eng-runtime): On it. Do we have an example request id or logs? 429s + throughput drop usually points at batcher backpressure or a scheduler regression.

support-ops: ticket #5467 — attached logs show many requests queued but batches remain tiny. Sample log: 
```
2026-03-17T09:12:21Z batcher: popped 1 req(s), tokens=36, batch_tokens=36, dispatch_delay_ms=240
2026-03-17T09:12:21Z batcher: popped 1 req(s), tokens=12, batch_tokens=12, dispatch_delay_ms=260
2026-03-17T09:12:22Z queue: depth=142, inflight=64, throttles=120/sec
```

omar (sre): That queue depth spike + tiny batch sizes smell like the continuous-batcher is dispatching early due to a tokens ceiling or quantum miscalc. Any recent config rollouts? :eyes:

carol (oncall): I rolled a scheduler tuning change two days ago to `scheduler.quantum_ms=2` during canary. That should help p99 latency, but maybe it interacts badly with `max_batch_tokens`. Reverting now possible if we confirm.

jess (eng-runtime): Ok let's gather: 1) check `max_batch_tokens` and `max_batch_delay_ms` on the pool 2) look for a rollout to batching/quantum 3) capture a short profiler of batch formation.

ryan (infra): I pulled the rollout history: change `scheduler.quantum_ms` -> 2 was deployed yesterday at 03:20 UTC, targeted all dedicated pools. Also a parameter `max_batch_tokens` was lowered from 4096 to 512 in the same PR for memory safety. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/3128

support-ops: That sounds plausible — customer load has many concurrent short prompts; lowering `max_batch_tokens` could cause many small batches and higher per-token overhead.

jess (eng-runtime): Repro steps for us: hit the dedicated endpoint with many parallel short requests (5-10 tokens) and measure `avg_batch_tokens` and `dispatch_delay_ms`. Use the stress harness: 
```bash
# run from internal harness host
./stress_client -e https://dedicated-us-west-2.prod.redwood/api/generate \n  -c 200 -r 50 --prompt "Summarize: x" --tokens 10
```
Check metrics: `redwood.batcher.avg_batch_tokens`, `redwood.batcher.dispatch_delay_ms`, `redwood.queue.depth`.

carol (oncall): I ran the harness in staging with the current prod flags and see `avg_batch_tokens ~ 8` where baseline should be ~240. Dispatch delay is under target which means batches are pushed early.

omar (sre): Root cause hypothesis: combined effect of 1) lowered `max_batch_tokens` (4096->512) and 2) scheduler.quantum_ms aggressive drop -> faster wakeups -> the continuous-batcher prematurely flushes small batches to meet latency, hurting throughput. Noisy-tenant case if one customer sends lots of tiny requests will dominate.

ryan (infra): Short mitigation: revert `max_batch_tokens` to 4096 for Dedicated pools + bump `scheduler.quantum_ms` back to 8ms for canary. Can roll as config-only change — low risk.

jess (eng-runtime): Agree. For next steps: - Rollback `max_batch_tokens` for us-west pools now (carol?) - Throttle noisy tenant via tenant-level fairness weights as stopgap - Add a metric alert for `avg_batch_tokens < 50` to catch regressions

carol (oncall): Rolling config revert to 4096 on `us-west-2-prod` now. Patch queued, will monitor. ETA ~4m.

sre-bot: Deploy started: revert-max-batch-tokens-4096 (#infra-rollback-435) -> 6 nodes targeted.

(3m later)

carol (oncall): Revert finished. Metrics: `avg_batch_tokens` jumped from 8 -> 210, queue depth dropping from 142 -> 18, throttles cleared. Customer reports p99 improved and 429 rate back to normal.

support-ops: Customer confirms recovery. Thanks team. assigning postmortem to eng-runtime to capture why PR bundled token limit + quantum change.

jess (eng-runtime): Will write quick postmortem and add a canary test: simulate high QPS small-prompts workload to ensure `max_batch_tokens` reductions don't degrade throughput. Also we'll gate `max_batch_tokens` changes behind a perf test.

omar (sre): Also recommend making `avg_batch_tokens` a tracked KPI per pool and add an automatic fallback that increases `max_batch_tokens` if avg batch tokens < threshold for >60s.

ryan (infra): Logging action items in #infra-ops with links to PR and metrics.

support-ops: closing on customer side. Thanks all :heart:
